subject: mathematics
question_text: Compute a × (b + c) + b × (c + a) + c × (a + b).

mark_split.label: Group the six terms into pairs
Show each pair is the zero vector
State the answer as the zero vector

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.75, chapter 7 PRODUCT OF VECTORS, Short Answer question 39. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1+1+1 split rewards the distributive expansion, the pairing, the cancellation rule, and the closing statement — the last mark is separate because the answer is the zero VECTOR and a student who writes the number 0 has not answered a question about cross products. ESTABLISHED ALGEBRAICALLY and CHECKED ON TWO CONCRETE TRIPLES. With a = i, b = j, c = k the three terms are k − j, i − k and j − i, which add to the zero vector. With a = i + 2j + 3k, b = 2i − j + k, c = i − k the three terms are (3, 9, −7), (−4, −2, 6) and (1, −7, 1), which also add to the zero vector; each of those three cross products was dotted with both of its own inputs and every one of the six dot products was 0 — for example (3, 9, −7)·a = 3 + 18 − 21 = 0 and (3, 9, −7)·(b + c) = 9 − 9 + 0 = 0. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B prints eight short answers of which the student writes any six, each worth 4 marks, under the 2026-27 pattern; Product of Vectors supplies at least one of those eight on almost every paper. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would simplify this — say what happens to the six terms after you expand.

steps.label: Expand the three brackets
steps.margin_note: First mark. The cross product distributes over addition, so each bracket splits into two terms. The order inside each term must be kept exactly as written.
steps.memory_tip: Expand like ordinary brackets, but never swap the two vectors inside a term.

recall.must_convey: That each bracket distributes into two terms, keeping the order inside each term.

steps.why: The cross product distributes over addition in the same way ordinary multiplication does, so every bracket splits into two terms. The order inside each term matters, because reversing it changes the sign.
common_mistakes: Writing a × (b + c) as (b + c) × a.
Adding b and c first and stopping there.

steps.label: Group the six terms into pairs
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Six terms, three pairs. Each term has a partner with the same two vectors in the opposite order.
steps.memory_tip: Look for the partner of each term — the same two letters, written the other way round.

recall.must_convey: That the six terms pair up as (a×b, b×a), (a×c, c×a) and (b×c, c×b).

steps.why: Each of the six terms has exactly one partner with the two vectors in the opposite order. Spotting those three pairs is the whole idea of the question.
common_mistakes: Pairing a×b with a×c, which are not reverses of each other.
Assuming a×b = b×a and cancelling the wrong terms.

steps.label: Show each pair is the zero vector
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Reversing a cross product reverses its direction but not its length, so a vector and its reverse add to the zero vector.
steps.memory_tip: y × x = −(x × y), so a reversed pair always adds to the zero vector.
lines: For any two vectors, y × x = −(x × y).

recall.must_convey: That y × x = −(x × y), so each of the three pairs adds to the zero vector.

steps.why: Reversing the order of a cross product reverses its direction but leaves its length alone, so a term and its reverse are opposite vectors. Opposite vectors add to the zero vector.
common_mistakes: Treating the result as the number zero at this stage.

steps.label: State the answer
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Three zero vectors add to the zero vector. Say vector, not number — every term in the sum was a cross product.
steps.memory_tip: The sum of cross products is a vector, so the answer is the zero vector, not the number zero.

steps.why: The sum of three zero vectors is the zero vector. The answer must be written as a vector, because every term added was a cross product and every cross product is a vector.
common_mistakes: Writing the answer as the number 0.
Leaving the answer as a×b + b×c + c×a.
